name: the-ring-fills-clockwise
description: The comet ring keeps its first phase and gains a second. Once bytes arrive the sweep stops and the ring fills clockwise from twelve o clock, with --fillang carrying the fraction as an angle. The read is taken from the cascade rather than from the sheet, because --fillang is set inline per element by loading-mark.js and only the computed value proves the push reached the row. A capture is kept beside it because the ring band's y moves with every sidebar size change, so no region assertion can be keyed to it.

actions.note: the second phase is entered on the first LoadProgressChanged, which lands after the commit and before the fixture's hold ends.

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.row.receiving, .fav.receiving'); if (!el) { return 'no receiving ring'; } const raw = getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--fillang').trim(); const deg = parseFloat(raw); if (!Number.isFinite(deg)) { return 'unreadable ' + raw; } return deg > 0 && deg <= 360 ? 'filling clockwise' : 'off ' + raw; })()

actions.note: RECORDED, NOT ASSERTED: the angle the run actually reached. The fraction is whatever Chromium reported at that instant, so pinning a number here would be a flake.

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.receiving > .brdr'); if (!el) { return 'no ring'; } const name = getComputedStyle(el, '::before').animationName; return name === 'none' || name === '' ? 'stopped' : 'still spinning ' + name; })()

actions.note: the fill phase ends with the load, so the ring goes back to the solid selected state.

assertions.desc: the reload put a row or a tile into the second phase, so the state under test was reached
THE MEASUREMENT: --fillang resolves to an angle inside the circle, so the conic fill has a real arc to draw.
the two phases do not run at once. A spinning comet under a static fill is the failure this catches.
the fill phase ends with the load rather than leaving a frozen arc on the row.
